title: Configuring GitHub Copilot for Agentic Workflows
objectives: Understand what agentic AI means in the context of software development
Enable and configure GitHub Copilot's agent mode in VS Code
Set up workspace-level Copilot settings for optimal agentic behavior
Verify your configuration with a live agentic task

sections.title: 🔍 What Are Agentic Workflows?
sections.content:
Traditional AI code assistants respond to a single prompt with a single suggestion. Agentic workflows go much further — the AI operates as an autonomous agent that can plan multi-step tasks, execute commands, read and write files, and iterate on its own output until the task is complete.

Think of it this way: a regular assistant answers questions, but an agent completes tasks. GitHub Copilot's agent mode transforms it from a code suggestion tool into a full development partner.

💡 Key Concepts

Agent Mode: Copilot autonomously plans, executes, and iterates on tasks. It can run terminal commands, edit multiple files, and fix its own errors.
Chat Mode: Standard Q&A — Copilot responds to prompts but doesn't take action.
Edit Mode: Copilot makes inline code changes you specify, but doesn't run or test them.

sections.title: 🛠️ Step-by-Step: Enable Agent Mode in VS Code
sections.content:
1

Install Prerequisites

Ensure you have VS Code 1.99+ and the GitHub Copilot extension (v1.250+). Open VS Code, go to Extensions (Ctrl+Shift+X), and search for "GitHub Copilot". Install or update to the latest version.

2

Enable Agent Mode in Settings

Open Settings (Ctrl+,), search for chat.agent.enabled, and ensure it is checked. This activates the agent mode toggle in the Copilot Chat panel.

3

Open Copilot Chat & Switch to Agent

Open Copilot Chat (Ctrl+Shift+I). At the bottom of the chat input, you'll see a mode dropdown. Switch it from "Chat" to "Agent".

4

Configure Workspace Settings

Create a .vscode/settings.json in your project root for workspace-specific Copilot settings. This ensures all team members share the same configuration.

sections.title: 🧪 Try It Yourself: First Agentic Task
sections.content: Let's verify your configuration with a simple agentic task. Open the Copilot Chat in agent mode and type the following prompt:

codeBlocks.title: Agentic Task: hello-agent
codeBlocks.code:
Create a new file called hello-agent.js that exports a function
greetUser(name) which returns a personalized greeting. Then create
a test file hello-agent.test.js with at least 3 test cases using
Jest. Run the tests and fix any failures.

sections.title: ✅ What to Look For
sections.content:
Watch how the agent plans the task, creates both files, installs Jest if needed, runs the tests, and fixes any issues — all autonomously.

✅ A successful agentic flow shows:

  • The agent's plan in the chat
  • File creation in your explorer
  • Terminal commands executing
  • Automatic error correction if tests fail

questions.text: What is the primary difference between Copilot's Agent mode and Chat mode?
options: Agent mode is faster at generating code
Agent mode can autonomously plan, execute commands, and iterate on tasks
Chat mode cannot understand natural language
Agent mode only works with Python projects
questions.explanation: Agent mode goes beyond answering questions — it autonomously plans multi-step tasks, runs terminal commands, edits files, and iterates until the task is complete.

questions.text: Which VS Code setting enables Copilot's agent mode?
questions.explanation: The setting 'chat.agent.enabled' in VS Code settings activates the agent mode toggle in the Copilot Chat panel.

questions.text: Where should workspace-level Copilot instructions be configured?
options: In the GitHub repository settings page
In the Copilot extension global settings only
questions.explanation: Workspace-level configurations go in .vscode/settings.json, which allows project-specific settings that can be shared across the team.

questions.text: You want the Copilot agent to automatically use TypeScript strict mode for all generated code. Which setting achieves this?
options: Add { "text": "Use TypeScript with strict mode enabled" } to github.copilot.chat.codeGeneration.instructions in .vscode/settings.json
Enable strict mode in the Copilot organization settings
questions.explanation: The codeGeneration.instructions array in .vscode/settings.json passes persistent instructions to the agent for every code generation request. This is how you enforce project-wide coding standards.

questions.text: An agent creates a file, runs tests, sees failures, and fixes them without you re-prompting. Which setting enables this self-correction loop?
questions.explanation: github.copilot.chat.agent.autoFix enables the agent to detect errors in its output (like failing tests) and automatically attempt to fix them, completing the iterative self-correction loop.
